paras: The threatened lynching of Fred Henderson took place at Canton, Kansas, in August 1881, when a mob clamored to lynch Henderson, a Black man charged with attempted rape. Henderson was acquitted at his preliminary hearing and returned to Emporia, and the Emporia weekly news, which had first reported the charge as his offense, declared him innocent.

Henderson, described as "a colored man who formerly resided at Emporia," was accused of attempted rape upon "an old lady of Canton." On a Thursday early in August, the Emporia authorities received a telegram from Canton saying he had started for Emporia and asking them to take him into custody.

The next day, ex-Marshal Fleming recognized Henderson as he passed in front of the Emporia court house and pointed him out to Marshal Johnson, who arrested him and lodged him in jail. In reporting the arrest, the Emporia weekly news added that "it is intimated that his case will be summarily disposed of" once he was back in Canton. He was taken to Canton on the charge, where, according to the paper's follow-up, "the mob was clamoring to lynch" him. The size of the mob, where it gathered and when are not stated in the coverage, and no attack on Henderson is reported.
Henderson was acquitted at his preliminary hearing and returned to Emporia by 18 August. No report of arrests or any official action against the mob appears in the coverage.

The episode appears only in two short local items in the Emporia weekly news, a week apart. The first treated the charge as fact, calling it "his offense" and Henderson "the fugitive," and passed on without comment the hint that he would be dealt with summarily. The second reversed course, stating that the man "whom the mob was clamoring to lynch, was perfectly innocent of the crime of which he was suspected." No Canton paper, wire dispatch or other Kansas report of the case appears in the coverage.

reader.title: Threatened lynching of Fred Henderson
bases: A mob clamored to lynch Henderson after he was charged with attempted rape, but no attack is reported and he was acquitted and released (A1, A2).

Henderson was not killed; the Emporia paper reports only that a mob of unstated size 'was clamoring to lynch' him over an attempted-rape charge before he was acquitted (A2), so this was a threatened lynching, not a completed one.
Both reports come from one paper, the Emporia weekly news, and the mob threat appears in only one sentence (A1, A2); no Canton or wire account was found.

accounts.label: Emporia weekly news, arrest report
accounts.gist: Henderson was arrested in Emporia on a telegram from Canton for attempted rape on an old lady, and it was 'intimated' his case would be 'summarily disposed of' on his return.

accounts.label: Emporia weekly news, follow-up
accounts.gist: Henderson was acquitted at his preliminary hearing; the mob that had clamored to lynch him had wanted an innocent man.

framing.detail: The Emporia paper first wrote of 'his offense' and the 'fugitive' as settled facts and passed on a hint of summary disposal, then a week later declared him 'perfectly innocent' and referred to the mob without approval.
